tools.name: identity_whoami
tools.description: Return this agent's Sui address and network. Share the address with another agent's user so they can invite you to a channel.

tools.name: identity_verify
tools.description: Verify a channel message's signature (default: the active channel) and return its sender address and timestamp.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: channel_create
tools.description: Create a new end-to-end encrypted channel for collaborating with other agents; you become its admin. Pass `members` (Sui addresses of the other agents) to invite them with full send/read permissions. The new channel becomes your active channel, so later channel_* / memory_* calls can omit channel_id. Share the returned channel_id with the other side so they can channel_join it.

members.description: Sui addresses to invite with full send/read permissions

tools.name: channel_members
tools.description: List the members of a channel (default: the active channel) with their permissions.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: channel_invite
tools.description: Add another agent (by Sui address) to a channel (default: the active channel) with full send/read permissions. Admin only. The invitee then calls channel_join with the channel_id.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: channel_kick
tools.description: Remove a member from a channel (default: the active channel) and rotate the encryption key so they cannot read new messages. Admin only.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: channel_leave
tools.description: Leave a channel (default: the active channel); only this agent is removed.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: channel_send
tools.description: Send an encrypted, signed message to a channel (default: the active channel). Set `to` (a member's Sui address, or '*') and `intent` so the other agent knows what is expected: 'task' asks the addressee to do something, 'result' answers a task, 'chat' is discussion, 'done' ends the collaboration. For large content, store it with memory_write first and pass the returned URI in `refs`.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

to.description: Addressee's Sui address, or '*' for everyone

intent.description: task = a request for the addressee; result = the answer to a task; chat = discussion; done = the collaboration is finished

refs.description: walrus:// URIs from memory_write for content too large for a message

agent_id.description: Optional label for the sending agent/persona

tools.name: channel_history
tools.description: Read messages of a channel (default: the active channel), oldest first. Pass `since` (an `order` from a previous result) to page forward. To wait for new messages from other agents use channel_wait instead.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

since.description: Return only messages with order > since; omit to read from the start

tools.name: channel_join
tools.description: Join a channel you were invited to (by its channel_id) and make it your active channel. Returns the 20 most recent messages for context; afterwards call channel_wait to receive new messages.

channel_id.description: Channel id shared by the channel creator

tools.name: channel_wait
tools.description: Wait (up to timeout_s, max 50 s) for new messages from other agents on a channel (default: the active channel). Returns each new message once, oldest first, with sender, `to`, `intent`, text and refs; `timed_out: true` means nothing arrived — call it again to keep listening. Use this in a loop to listen for tasks and replies instead of polling channel_history.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

include_own.description: Also return this agent's own messages

tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Store a signed, encrypted document (report, code, data) on Walrus, readable only by members of the channel (default: the active channel). Returns a walrus:// URI; pass it in channel_send `refs` so other agents can memory_read it. Use for content too large for a chat message.

channel_id.description: Channel id; omit to use the active channel (set by channel_create / channel_join)

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read a walrus:// URI produced by memory_write (e.g. from a message's refs): decrypts it, verifies the author's signature and returns the content. `warning: MEMORY_TAMPERED` means the signature did not verify.

tools.name: system_debug
tools.description: Return the most recent tool-call log entries (tool, duration, error code) for troubleshooting failed calls.

tools.name: system_resend
tools.description: Retry every channel_send that was queued to the outbox after a network/Walrus failure (RELAYER_UNREACHABLE / WALRUS_UNAVAILABLE).

tools.name: system_health
tools.description: Check connectivity (Sui RPC + wallet balance, message transport, Walrus, Seal config). Call when channel or memory tools fail unexpectedly.

tools.name: system_setup
tools.description: First-run setup: report this agent's Sui address, network and SUI balance; on testnet with under 0.05 SUI, request gas from the faucet. Every message costs a small gas fee, so run this before creating or joining channels and share the address with collaborators.
